targetAudience.primary: Architects and governance owners of long-lived digital employees
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands memory retrieval, provenance, model judgment, and recovery.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A later summary or semantic classification can overwrite or hide the only evidence future decisions depend on.

whyNow: ROAM provides fresh primary-study evidence for keeping atomic observations immutable while relation judgments and active retrieval views evolve.

externalHook.description: A later interpretation becomes the only surviving truth even though the source observation still matters for audit and recovery.

coreProposition: Long-lived memory should make evidence harder to mutate than interpretation by separating immutable observations, relation decisions, active retrieval views, and recoverable evidence history.

originalValue.description: Separates observation identity, relation-decision identity, active-view identity, and evidence-history identity so semantic errors remain reversible.

readerTakeaway: Preserve source observations and transformation provenance independently from the active retrieval view; rebuild interpretations without recreating evidence from summaries.

supported: The study stores incoming observations as immutable atomic records.
Semantic relation labels drive deterministic precedence after classification.
Active primary and fused views differ from the preserved evidence substrate.
Reported benchmark and ablation results support the tested memory mechanism.
unsupported: A claim that the active view is always true
A claim that immutable storage supplies execution authorization
A proof of distributed crash consistency or exactly-once ingestion
uncertain: How much demoted evidence audit retrieval should expose
How concurrent contradictions should be ordered

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from public primary research and remains independently useful.

decisionReason: The evidence supports a bounded memory-state architecture while preserving authorization and production limits.
